WWAggr ensemble drift detector

Source: R/dfr_wwaggr.R
dfr_wwaggr.Rd

Monitors a stream with an ensemble of change point models (cpd_ensemble(), preferably calibrated with cpd_calibrate()): every member scores the observations as they arrive, the scores are aggregated by WWAggr (Stepikin et al., 2025) or by a naive aggregation (wwaggr()), and a drift is reported when the aggregated score exceeds threshold. Since the members are trained on sequences of the monitored features, it detects changes of their distribution (virtual concept drift).

Usage

dfr_wwaggr(
  ensemble,
  threshold = 0.5,
  method = c("wasserstein", "mmd", "mean", "min", "max", "median", "quantile"),
  window_size = 3,
  anchor = c("prev", "start", "combined"),
  p = 1,
  kernel = c("rbf", "multiscale"),
  bandwidth = NULL,
  q = 0.5,
  target_feat = NULL,
  horizon = NULL
)

Arguments

ensemble

A cpd_ensemble.

threshold

Alarm threshold on the aggregated score. With calibrated members and the 1-Wasserstein distance, the paper finds that a threshold near 0.5 is close to the best one.

method, window_size, anchor, p, kernel, bandwidth, q

Aggregation, as in wwaggr().

target_feat

Names of the columns fed to the members, in the order of training. NULL (default) uses the feature names of the ensemble, or every numeric column when it has none.

horizon

If set, the members and the aggregation restart every horizon observations, so that the stream is read as consecutive sequences of the training length. NULL (default) restarts them only after a drift.

Value

dfr_wwaggr object. After fit(), drifter_output holds, for every observation, the aggregated score (score, NA when there is none) and whether a drift was reported (drift).

Details

The members score each observation online, as on whole sequences: the LSTM models (indid()) update their state; the representation models (tscp2(), ts2vec()) compare the embeddings of the last two windows of window observations (every step observations, with the exponential smoothing alpha), so they have no score for the first 2 * window - 1 observations of a sequence. The aggregation starts when all members have a score, and its score at an observation compares the window of the window_size previous scores with the anchor (see wwaggr()). After a drift, the members and the aggregation restart. Rows with missing values are skipped.

References

Stepikin, A., Romanenkova, E. and Zaytsev, A. (2025). WWAggr: A window Wasserstein-based aggregation for ensemble change point detection. 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM), 1535-1544. doi:10.1109/ICDM65498.2025.00163

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
make <- function(n) {
  change <- sample(5:24, n, replace = TRUE)
  change[seq_len(n / 2)] <- 25
  x <- t(vapply(change, function(c) stats::rnorm(24, ifelse(seq_len(24) < c, 0, 3)), numeric(24)))
  list(x = x, labels = t(vapply(change, function(c) (seq_len(24) >= c) * 1, numeric(24))))
}
train <- make(96)
ensemble <- cpd_ensemble_fit(train$x, train$labels, model = "bce", n_models = 3, epochs = 10,
                             learning_rate = 0.01, seed = 1)
ensemble <- cpd_calibrate(ensemble, train$x, train$labels)
stream <- data.frame(value = c(stats::rnorm(15), stats::rnorm(15, 3)))
detector <- fit(dfr_wwaggr(ensemble, window_size = 2), stream)
which(detector$drifter_output$drift == 1)
#> [1] 19
